solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Say nothing: manage with knowledge that's much reduced?

parts.note: SH is the call for silence
to run a business is to manage it
ken means range of knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: Advice to keep quiet and get by on very little know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN is an old Scots word for knowledge, kept alive by the phrase 'beyond my ken'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shrunken has become a lot smaller, the past participle of shrink used as an adjective.

clue.text: Pram zone zoo's organised for female singer

indicators.note: things organised are put into a new order, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A baby area at the zoo is being set up for a woman who sings.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in zoo's is ignored, so its S joins the letters to shuffle; the two Zs are a strong hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A mezzo-soprano is a voice type between soprano and contralto, usually sung by women.

clue.text: Cases of cider, ice-cream and Barolo for Christmas

indicators.note: a case is the outside casing of something, so only the edge letters of each word count

parts.note: first and last letters of the drink
first and last letters of the dessert
first and last letters of the wine

explanation.surface: A shopping list of crates of drink and dessert for the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like crates of drink, but it means the outside letters of each item; Barolo is an Italian red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimbo is informal British slang for the Christmas holiday, used jokily in speech.

clue.text: Girl endlessly tries to grab one kiss

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
grabbing something means holding it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the word tries minus its last letter
I is the Roman numeral one
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A girl keeps trying to snatch a single kiss from someone.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIE, with its end trimmed, wraps around I and X, the numeral one and the kiss sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Trixie is a female given name, so it is an example of a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Place in Austria making razors for paring down

indicators.note: paring trims away the outer parts, leaving a core inside the words

parts.note: runs from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: An Austrian town whose industry is producing blades for shaving or trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: Razors really are for paring, so the phrase reads naturally while telling you to cut the fodder down to a middle run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Graz is Austria's second-largest city, capital of the state of Styria in the south-east.

clue.text: Exclamation of alarm as a horde assembled

indicators.note: things assembled are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cries out in fright as a crowd gathers menacingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembled' fits a gathering horde, but it is the signal to rearrange the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild spoken cry expressing dismay or worry when something goes wrong.

clue.text: Inter again later the club you swear by, ultimately!

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only final letters are kept

parts.words: later the club you swear by
parts.note: the final letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: A football fan vows loyalty to their team, even as far as burial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inter' looks like the Milan football club, matching the club in the surface, but it is the verb meaning to bury.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body, so interring again means putting it back in the grave a second time.

clue.text: Aircraft to lift alien's coat

parts.note: a bomber is a military plane
to jack up a car is to lift it
ET is the film's extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A plane arrives to collect an extraterrestrial's outer garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after alien is a link meaning 'is', joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomber jacket is a short padded coat with a gathered waist, modelled on aircrew flying gear.

clue.text: Variable IQ reflected after taking in university pub event?

indicators.note: placing one part after another puts it later in the line
a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front
taking something in means admitting it inside

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university
algebra names unknowns x, y and z

explanation.surface: Intelligence on show at a student bar's trivia night.
explanation.walkthrough: Mathematical variables in crosswords are X, Y or Z; here Z comes last, after the turned IQ has swallowed U.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub quiz is a trivia contest held in a bar, a classic example of an evening event at the local.

clue.text: Make the most of revolutionary mix in corn

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: maize is corn

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Get the best from a radical new blend of cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary mix' sounds like a novel blend, but revolutionary just turns the word round before it goes inside the corn.
explanation.definitionFit: To maximize something is to exploit it fully, getting the greatest possible use from it.

clue.text: Kiss Pole madly in winter sports setting

indicators.note: acting madly is acting wildly and out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A passionate embrace with a Polish person at a winter resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a nationality or a ski pole; both words are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski slope is the snowy hillside where people go downhill skiing, the place for that winter activity.

clue.text: Greek character with ukulele originally more musical

parts.note: pi is a Greek letter

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the instrument

explanation.surface: A Greek person with a ukulele seems more musical than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More musical' reads as a comparative adjective but means 'the musical word for more'; più is Italian, as used in score directions like più forte.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian score markings use this word meaning more, as in a direction to play louder or faster.

clue.text: Eye venue for return, regularly — experiencing this?

definitions.text: Eye venue for return, regularly — experiencing this?

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even-placed letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone eyes up a place they long to get back to, wondering what they feel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a hint: eyeing up somewhere you want to return to is green-eyed longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is resentful longing for what another has, the green-eyed monster that covets with the eyes.

clue.text: Our vet is upset, becoming glassy

indicators.note: upsetting things knocks them out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Our distressed veterinarian's eyes are glazing over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as the vet's emotional state, but it signals the rearrangement of the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitreous comes from Latin for glass and describes something resembling glass in look or texture.

clue.text: A biscuit or photo? It's the same thing!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thin crisp ginger biscuit, or a quick casual photograph
second meaning: the shout in the card game when two matching cards appear

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is itself two senses, a crisp biscuit and a casual photo; the second is the card game where you call out on spotting a matching pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a brittle biscuit, a quick photograph, and the cry made in a children's card-matching game.

clue.text: MP in France I involved in projects that take off immediately?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'things that take off immediately'

indicators.note: being involved in something means being caught up inside it

parts.note: juts means sticks out
taken as written
je is French for I

explanation.surface: A politician over in France is caught up in schemes that get going at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projects' wants to be schemes, but it is the verb juts, wrapped round MP and the French I.
explanation.definitionFit: Jump jets are aircraft capable of vertical takeoff, needing no runway to get airborne at once.

clue.text: Yes German females like oranges!

parts.note: ja is German for yes
F is female, doubled for the plural
as means like, in comparisons

explanation.surface: German women enthusiastically approve of citrus fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubling a letter makes a plural in abbreviations, so FF stands for females.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaffas are a variety of sweet seedless orange named after the port of Jaffa.

clue.text: Evil intent of maiden, a girl in wonderland

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
the heroine of Lewis Carroll's story

explanation.surface: A sinister plot by a young woman lost in a fantasy world.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to cause harm, a synonym for ill will or wicked purpose.

clue.text: Very unpleasant fag would, when put out

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed or displaced from its proper state

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cigarette smells foul as it is being stubbed out.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a fag is a cigarette, so 'put out' looks like extinguishing it rather than rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: God-awful is an informal intensifier meaning extremely bad or dreadful.

clue.text: One arranged to keep ten cattle

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside
arranging things sets them in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: One person is set up to look after ten cows.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters of one are rearranged, then the Roman ten slips between the first and second.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are domestic bovines, especially those used for pulling ploughs, so they are cattle.

clue.text: Charlie cut a toffee, perhaps

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: Someone named Charlie breaks off a piece of a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a toffee is one kind of a chewy sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A chew is a soft, chewy sweet, and toffee is a typical instance of that confectionery.

clue.text: City some discover on Adige

indicators.note: some means only part, so a run of letters is taken from inside the words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A city that some travellers find on a particular Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adige is a river in northern Italy, and the answer city really stands on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Verona is a city in the Veneto region of Italy, the setting of Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Money order spoken for by vet or E European?

indicators.note: spoken words are heard rather than read, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: to vet is to check, and a Czech is from eastern Europe; both are said the same way

explanation.surface: Who pays for things this way: a veterinarian, or someone from Eastern Europe?
explanation.walkthrough: Two sound-alikes are offered: check, meaning vet, and Czech, an eastern European; either pronounced gives the bank document.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque is a written order instructing a bank to pay money from an account.
